protocol.question: Does actual database enforcement preserve tenant and access-level eligibility for retrieval and direct reads?
alternatives: global RLS table and GIN index
separate databases with own tables/GIN indexes; same server/CPU/WAL/admin

retriever.indexUse: Record actual role EXPLAIN; small data may use sequential scan. Index existence is not evidence that planner used it.

protocol.matrix: 4 principals × 7 authored query terms × 2 layouts = 56 requests. Gold document IDs authored before native execution. Not blind evaluation.
protocol.security: Login as each effective non-owner, non-superuser, NOBYPASSRLS role. Policies bind session_user to admin-maintained principal table. Never trust GUC tenant or tenant supplied in question.
protocol.metrics: Eligible document recall@3 for nonempty gold; null for empty gold. Count unexpected returned IDs separately. No latency benchmark, generated answer, semantic judge or ANN claim.
protocol.preservation: Refuse to overwrite capture. On execution failure save failure artifact; do not silently retry favorable selections. A new protocol/path is required for changed inputs.

runtime.network: loopback ephemeral port; temporary synthetic databases only
runtime.authentication: trust ONLY in disposable loopback lab; not a deployment configuration
